macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: Global stocks slip, Wall Street futures lower as investors await Iran sanctions details
items.summary: Reuters reported that global equities were mostly lower, with European stocks down 0.1% early and U.S. S&P 500 futures off 0.2% and Nasdaq futures down 0.7%. The move came as markets waited for details on threatened U.S. sanctions on Iran and monitored rising trade tensions with Canada.

items.title: Gold extends rally to a three-month high on dollar weakness and fiscal worries
items.summary: Gold rose to its highest level in more than three months, with spot prices around $4,636 and U.S. gold futures near $4,691-$4,694. Analysts cited a softer dollar, concern over U.S. fiscal sustainability, and expectations for upcoming U.S. inflation data and a Fed Chair speech.

items.title: U.S. futures edge lower as 30-year Treasury yield tops 5.3%
items.summary: U.S. stock futures fell as the 30-year Treasury yield climbed above 5.3%, its highest level in nearly two decades, while long-term yields also rose in Japan, France, and Germany. Traders continued to focus on fiscal pressures and the potential impact on risk assets.

items.title: Dollar hovers near multi-month lows ahead of policy speeches and Iran sanctions update
items.summary: The U.S. dollar remained under pressure near multi-month lows as investors reacted to the Treasury's plan to increase buybacks of longer-dated bonds and awaited new sanctions details on Iran. Market participants also looked ahead to policy signals from the U.S. and Japan later in the week.

items.title: Alibaba shares slide after large share offer and AI-spending concerns
items.summary: Hong Kong-listed Alibaba fell about 9% after launching a $10.2 billion share offer, with investors also worrying about the payback from its heavy AI investment spending. The weakness added to the broader risk-off tone across Asian markets.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin tops $79,000 as ETF inflows and U.S. regulation optimism fuel rally
items.summary: Bitcoin briefly moved above $79,000 before easing back, supported by institutional demand, ETF inflows, and optimism around the CLARITY Act. The move came alongside broader strength across major crypto assets over the past 24 hours.

items.title: Crypto market sees sharp volatility after flash crash and heavy liquidations
items.summary: A weekend flash crash wiped roughly $100 billion from the crypto market in minutes, with XRP falling 37% and more than $1.7 billion liquidated in 24 hours. Other reports also cited nearly $3 billion in liquidations across the market as leverage was flushed out.

items.title: EU sanctions package takes effect, banning transactions with 11 crypto-related platforms
items.summary: The European Union’s latest Russia sanctions package introduced a transaction ban on 11 crypto-related service platforms, including HTX, EXMO, and BitPapa. The restrictions took effect on August 23 under the bloc’s 21st sanctions package.

items.title: U.S. OCC grants preliminary approval for Trump-linked crypto bank trust charter
items.summary: The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency conditionally approved a national trust bank charter for World Liberty Financial’s trust company, a venture linked to Donald Trump and his family. The approval marks a notable U.S. regulatory development for a crypto-affiliated firm.

items.title: Phantom to end Sui network support next month
items.summary: Phantom said it will stop supporting the Sui network on September 24, giving users one month to migrate assets. The move is one of the more notable project-level developments in the past 24 hours.

items.title: Fasset raises $68 million in Series C to expand stablecoin-focused neobank
items.summary: Stablecoin network neobank Fasset reportedly raised $68 million in a Series C round led by Japan’s SBI, valuing the company at $1 billion. The deal highlights continued venture interest in stablecoin and payments infrastructure.

items.title: South Korea expands pressure on unregistered crypto firms and Polymarket access
items.summary: Recent coverage highlighted South Korean regulatory action targeting unregistered crypto activity and a separate move to block Polymarket access. These steps add to the ongoing global tightening around crypto platforms and prediction markets.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: GTA 6 leak saga escalates as Rockstar/Take-Two seek leaker identity
items.summary: Reports say new Grand Theft Auto VI gameplay clips surfaced again, prompting Take-Two to pursue the alleged leaker’s identity through Discord records and legal action. Multiple outlets also note Rockstar remains committed to its scheduled November 19, 2026 launch window.

items.title: Rockstar says a GTA 6 extended trailer is coming soon
items.summary: A roundup of upcoming game news says Rockstar has announced an extended GTA 6 preview scheduled to premiere on Netflix on August 28, adding to the week’s surge of official and unofficial Grand Theft Auto VI activity.

items.title: EA shuts down more NHL servers
items.summary: ETtoday reports that EA has closed the servers for NHL 22 and NHL 23, continuing a broader pattern of game service shutdowns in the industry.

items.title: The Duskbloods network test faces immediate problems
items.summary: ETtoday says the first network test for The Duskbloods ran into login failures, forcing the official team to cancel the session shortly after it began.

items.title: Chinese team All Gamers wins the Esports World Cup
items.summary: All Gamers defeated Team Falcons to win the Esports World Cup title in Paris, ending the Saudi team’s bid for another championship.

items.title: Double Fine outlines a new post-Microsoft future
items.summary: Double Fine says it will return to crowdfunding and let backers help choose prototypes, marking a notable shift in its development strategy after leaving Microsoft’s umbrella.

items.title: How to Fish reaches 1 million copies sold in two days
items.summary: 3DNews reports that the game How to Fish sold one million copies within its first two days, making it one of the most notable release milestones of the day.

items.title: Heatwarped announced as a new old-school racing game
items.summary: 3DNews says Heatwarped has been announced as an arcade racer inspired by Need for Speed Underground 2, and the reveal has drawn strong fan reaction.

items.title: Paradox’s new game Afterworld reportedly leaked
items.summary: A social post cited in search results claims Paradox’s unannounced game Afterworld was accidentally leaked via Discord and the company’s official forum.
